summary: Program windows: workbench/windows_x11.py reads the open windows from the X11 window properties (_NET_CLIENT_LIST, _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW, _NET_WM_NAME/WM_NAME, WM_CLASS, _NET_WM_PID, _NET_WM_STATE/WM_STATE, _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE, WM_TRANSIENT_FOR, WM_PROTOCOLS, _NET_WM_ICON) through ctypes on libX11, with xprop as the fallback reader and a bare-X fallback (root children + input focus) when no window manager keeps the list; it brings a window forward (_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW), minimises (WM_CHANGE_STATE iconic) and closes politely (_NET_CLOSE_WINDOW, only to an app that takes WM_DELETE_WINDOW; never a kill), each answer saying asked and verified; observe() gives Kasandra plain observation records for K2 (the windows, the active one, and events such as 'a new window appeared' / 'a new dialog appeared' with titles). workbench/windows_strip_qt.py is the slim strip directly under the head band, shown only while an app window is open: icon (S2 catalogue, else the window's own icon, else the WM_CLASS words / a letter tile) and the title cut short; the active one marked with a ▸, a rule and the word; right-click Bring forward, Minimise, Close (polite); "⋯ N more" when crowded; Graphite's own windows never listed as apps, Graphite's open dialogs kept reachable apart at the right end. Woken by PropertyNotify on its X socket, with a 3 s light poll as backstop. Without X it says "no window list on this computer" and why, and the window is unchanged.

decisions: No Kernel operations registered: observe() is the plain function the coordinator named for K2; so engineering_kernel/cli, activity observers and the registry record are untouched (record_registry only records operations/settings/job tools).

The strip reads X only when Graphite's own window is on X (Qt platform xcb). Offscreen (the tests, the window checks, a DISPLAY set beside offscreen) it stays hidden and says why ('Graphite's window is not on the X display here'), so no existing offscreen check sees a taller head or touches the owner's X.

Polite close is sent only to an app whose WM_PROTOCOLS has WM_DELETE_WINDOW: Fluxbox answers _NET_CLOSE_WINDOW for a client without it by killing the client, so Graphite says "this app cannot be asked to close politely" instead. Nothing is ever killed.

With no window manager keeping _NET_CLIENT_LIST (bare X, or a non-EWMH manager), the list falls back to the root's children (WM_STATE, else mapped and named) and the active window to the input focus; minimise then says there is no window manager to keep a minimised window.

Icons: S2's apps_catalog (not in this tree; guarded import of scan()/icon_path(), matched by StartupWMClass, desktop id, or Exec program against WM_CLASS) first, then the window's own _NET_WM_ICON (read once), else the WM_CLASS words (a letter tile when the entry is narrow).

Graphite's own windows are those of this process (pid + host) or Graphite's own X ids; they are never listed among the apps. Graphite's open dialogs (Qt Dialog/Window top-levels other than the main window) stand apart at the strip's right end with Graphite's mark; one press raises and activates them.

A press on an entry always brings it forward (it does not toggle minimise); Minimise and Close are on the right-click. The active entry: ▸ shape + rule + bolder ink + "active" in its tooltip/accessible name; minimised: brackets + word.

Entries are painted by the strip (exact widths, right elision) in the look's own chrome font; the strip starts at the middle column's edge under the menus with a quiet "Windows" caption over the left column, and uses the whole width when crowded; the rest fold into "⋯ N more".
On-screen words say "app windows", never "programs"; no keyboard shortcut appears in any of the strip's words.

Event-driven reading: the strip's Hub (one per process) watches its own X connection's socket (QSocketNotifier) and re-reads 120 ms after a relevant PropertyNotify; a 3 s poll is the backstop. libX11 reads run on the window thread (a few round trips per window); the display is opened, and any xprop reading runs, on a thread.
findings_for_the_coordinator: This container lacks the Qt xcb platform's libraries (libxcb-cursor0, libxkbcommon-x11-0, libxcb-icccm4, libxcb-image0, libxcb-keysyms1, libxcb-render-util0, libxcb-xkb1, libxcb-util1). For the Xvfb runs they were downloaded with apt-get download and extracted (not installed) into b100/S3/xcblibs/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to it to run Graphite with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb under Xvfb. INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh already names libxcb-cursor0 for the ThinkPad.

No window manager exists here (no Fluxbox): the EWMH path was exercised against a stand-in EWMH manager written for the smoke (b100/S3/xworld.py), not Fluxbox. The xprop fallback was not run (xprop is not installed); only its parser was exercised with canned xprop output.

When an app window covers Graphite's main window, the strip (part of Graphite's window) is behind it; the way back to Graphite is Fluxbox's own (its keys) or minimising/closing the app. A later slice may want Graphite reachable from above the apps (a dock-type window or struts).

K2: the window controller is windows_x11.shared() (activate/minimise/close(window, wait) -> {asked, verified, how, reason}); these run today only on the owner's press in the strip; any use by Kasandra must pass K3's grant. observe(since) -> {tool, kind, observed, observed_at, basis, available, reason, source, manager, complete, windows, active, events, seq}; reading a title is an observation, inferring a 'Save changes?' prompt is K2's to mark inferred.

Merge: shell2.py hunks are in TopBar.place (just after first_row.setGeometry) and Shell2.install (just after the TopBar is made); P1 and S2 also edit TopBar.place and Shell2.install, 10 to 40 lines away (no overlapping lines seen in their current patches). desk_qt.apply has one changed line.
not_done: Nothing ran on the ThinkPad, under Fluxbox, or with real apps; nothing was tested in the owner's sense.
The xprop fallback was not run end to end (xprop absent); wmctrl/xdotool acting paths not run.
No Day-look frames (P2 has not landed in this tree).
Kasandra's column does not yet say anything about windows (her observation is offered through observe() for K2).
release_note: The open app windows now show in a slim strip under the head: each with its icon and title, the active one marked; one press brings a window forward, and a right-click minimises it or asks it to close (the app may ask to save; nothing is forced). Graphite's own dialogs stay reachable at the strip's right end. Without X11 the strip stays away and says there is no window list on this computer.
